candidates.title: §9's receipt schema and gate_review option list omit the new Reason field/choice
candidates.detail: §9 ("Gates and receipts") shows the receipt JSON shape and explains `severities` in its own paragraph when that field was added, but says nothing about the new `Receipt.Reason`/`Status.Reason` fields (gate.go) that now carry the backend's error explanation through to the gate_review question. candidates.title: Fixed-point design's verdict table still says the error row is "unchanged"
candidates.detail: The §3 table row `| error | — | unchanged: ask gate_review. |` and the §4 edge-case row at line 141 (`revise on the plan gate, or on a blocking/reject/error spec receipt | No event written; today's re-arm behaviour, unchanged.`) both describe the error verdict as still offering `revise` with the old re-arm behaviour. The diff's questionGateReviewErrored (internal/decide/questions.go) removes `revise` entirely for an error verdict and replaces it with a new `retry` choice that writes nothing and just tells the session to re-run the reviewer. Task 8's only edit to this file adds one sentence after this table (about carried findings), so the table itself and the edge-case row were left describing behaviour the diff just removed. A reader of this design doc would still expect `revise` to be offered on an errored spec review.

candidates.title: alignmentLine reuse breaks loadCommitMessage's "skipped leaves message unchanged" contract
candidates.detail: alignmentLine(a) now returns a non-empty string ("skipped", "N clauses awaiting confirmation", or "N clauses confirmed, verdicts pending") for states that previously produced "". internal/cli/cmd_next.go:539-552 loadCommitMessage explicitly reuses this same alignmentLine (per its own doc comment, unmodified in this diff) and relies on it returning "" whenever there are no verdict artifacts: 'No verdict artifacts (the audit is disabled, skipped, or has not run yet) leaves the message unchanged.' That contract is now broken for the reachable 'explicitly skipped' path: takt answer --gate agent_invalid --choice skip → skipAlignment(bdir, st) sets alignment.json's Skipped=true; decidePlan's ClausesPresent/ClausesConfirmed/VerdictsPresent facts all become true via the `|| a.Skipped` OR (internal/cli/facts.go:78-80), so the plan→execute transition proceeds immediately and loadCommitMessage is called with a.Skipped=true. alignmentLine now hits `case a.Skipped: return gateSkipped` and returns "skipped" (non-empty), so the commit subject/body now gets " — alignment: skipped" appended, directly contradicting the still-present, unmodified doc comment and the existing behaviour TestLoadCommitMessageOmitsAlignmentWhenAbsent pins for the 'no verdict artifacts' cases (that test only covers the fully-absent alignment.json case, not the explicit-skip case, so it does not catch this). The two other new non-empty branches ('N clauses awaiting confirmation' / 'N clauses confirmed, verdicts pending') cannot actually be reached from decidePlan's transition gate, so only the Skipped branch is a live regression, but it is a real, untested one.

candidates.title: alignmentLine's new non-empty branches break loadCommitMessage's documented 'no verdicts → unchanged' contract
candidates.detail: Task 4 rewrote alignmentLine (used by both status and, per its own doc comment at cmd_status.go:593, by cmd_next.go's loadCommitMessage) so the `Skipped` case now returns the literal "skipped" instead of "". loadCommitMessage (internal/cli/cmd_next.go:524-553) treats an empty alignmentLine result as "no verdict artifacts (the audit is disabled, skipped, or has not run yet) — leave the message unchanged" (its own doc comment says so verbatim) and otherwise appends " — alignment: <line>" to the plan→execute commit subject/body. skipAlignment (internal/cli/cmd_answer.go:307-314) writes alignment.json with Skipped=true and no verdicts, and decide.go's decidePlan (internal/decide/decide.go:331-341) treats Skipped as satisfying ClausesPresent/ClausesConfirmed/VerdictsPresent, so the run proceeds straight to ActLoadPlan without ever gaining verdicts. The next `takt next` therefore reaches loadCommitMessage with a non-nil, Skipped alignment digest, and the plan→execute commit now reads "...— alignment: skipped" — contradicting loadCommitMessage's own documented behaviour and permanently altering commit history for a path task 4 never mentions touching. No test exercises this: TestLoadCommitMessageOmitsAlignmentWhenAbsent (internal/cli/cmd_next_test.go:346) only covers alignment fully disabled (statusAlignment returns nil), not the skipped-with-clauses case.

candidates.title: alignmentVerdictLine grows unrequested unknown-verdict handling
candidates.detail: Task 4's brief specifies alignmentLine's four cases (skipped / awaiting confirmation / confirmed-pending-verdicts / today's counts line) but says nothing about handling verdict words outside alignmentVerdictOrder. The diff adds a `seen` map plus a second pass that collects and sort.Strings' any unrecognised verdict word into a `rest` bucket (lines 616-633) — extra state and a second loop to defend against an auditor emitting a word the fixed order doesn't know. It's a reasonable robustness fix (previously such words were silently dropped) but it is scope creep beyond what the task asked for in a diff whose other status changes are otherwise minimal and tightly scoped to the brief. Flagging for awareness rather than blocking — the added complexity is small and self-contained.

candidates.title: alignmentVerdictLine's "unknown verdict" bucket is untested
candidates.detail: The refactor into alignmentVerdictLine adds a new branch (lines 624-633) that buckets and sorts any verdict word outside alignmentVerdictOrder rather than silently dropping it — a genuinely new code path per the doc comment ("nothing validates the auditor's word"). No test in internal/cli/cmd_status_test.go supplies an alignment.json verdict outside {covered, narrowed, dropped, widened, contradicted}, so this branch (and its sort.Strings ordering) has zero coverage.

candidates.title: PlanGate.Reason wiring only exercised indirectly, not through gatherGateFacts
candidates.detail: Both SpecGate and PlanGate literals in gatherGateFacts gain `Reason: s.Reason` (lines 135-137 and 143-145). The spec-gate branch is covered end-to-end by TestAnswerRetryOnAnErroredGateWritesNothingAndClearsIt (internal/cli/cmd_answer_retry_test.go), which plants a real error receipt and drives it through gate.Compute → gatherGateFacts → decide → question. The plan-gate branch's Reason threading is only checked via decide_test.go's TestTheGateReviewAskCarriesTheReceiptsReason/plan subtest, which constructs `decide.GateStatus{Verdict: "error", Reason: "x"}` directly and never calls gatherGateFacts or gate.Compute — so a bug specifically in facts.go's plan-gate literal (e.g. a typo omitting `Reason: s.Reason`) would not be caught by any test.

candidates.title: Two near-identical 'review errored, retry it' options use different verbs
candidates.detail: The new questionGateReviewErrored's retry option is labelled "Re-run the review (Recommended)" (questions.go:166), while the pre-existing questionReviewError (task-review-errored-during-close-wave gate, questions.go:325) uses "Retry the review (Recommended)" for the same underlying concept (a review that errored, offering to run it again). Both use choiceRetry and both are the sole recommended option for an errored review; the label text should match or the divergence should be explained, since a user comparing the two gates has no way to tell the wording difference means anything.

candidates.title: Adopted-branch "pr" recommendation label has no test
candidates.detail: questionBranchFinish's adopted-branch early return now does `pr.Label += suffixRecommended` (line 409), a new behaviour — before this diff the adopted branch never marked any option "(Recommended)". TestQuestionBranchFinishRecommendsAChoosableOption (internal/decide/finish_test.go) only covers the non-adopted merge-blocked/merge-allowed cases; the existing adopted-branch assertion in TestBranchFinishOptions (finish_test.go:227-232) checks only option order/choice, never the label text. No test would catch a regression that dropped the suffix or duplicated it in the adopted path.

candidates.title: Dead fallback in FollowUp.Key() for an error json.Marshal cannot produce
candidates.detail: Key() marshals a []any of only strings, ints and nil (see lines 90-97); json.Marshal cannot fail for those types (it only errors on channels, funcs, complex numbers, cyclic references or unsupported types), and the comment at lines 100-102 says as much ("Unreachable"). The fmt.Sprintf("%v", parts) fallback is therefore a legacy-style defensive branch that can never execute — a dead fallback per the over-engineering rubric (item 4). Not harmful, but it adds a branch and an unreachable format-based key-rendering path that will never be exercised by any test. Low priority: could simply be `b, _ := json.Marshal(parts); return string(b)` with a one-line comment noting why the error is ignored.
